nws.title: Weather Service watches and warnings
nws.detail: Nothing for Western New York right now.

ao.title: Arctic Oscillation: is cold air escaping?
ao.detail: Model average goes as low as -2.0 (Nov 12) and as high as +0.0. Below -2 = cold air can escape south. Above +2.5 = cold stays up north.

nao.title: North Atlantic Oscillation: is cold air steered our way?
nao.detail: Model average goes as low as -1.5 (Nov 14) and as high as -0.2. Below -1.5 = cold air gets steered into the East.

cpc610.title: NOAA 6–10 day outlook for Buffalo
cpc610.detail: Nov 15–Nov 19: 40% chance of being warmer than normal.

cpc814.title: NOAA 8–14 day outlook for Buffalo
cpc814.detail: Nov 17–Nov 23: 70% chance of being warmer than normal.

erie.title: Lake Erie water temperature
erie.detail: Nov 9: 6°F warmer than normal (53°F). Record for the date: 58.9°F (2024). Warmer water = more fuel for lake-effect snow.

vortex.title: Will the polar vortex break down?
vortex.detail: In 31 of 31 runs of the American weather model, the spinning winds over the Arctic stop and reverse within 16 days, as early as Nov 11. That can send Arctic air south 1 to 3 weeks later. Yesterday: 100%.

noreaster.title: Nor'easter in the next 10 days?
noreaster.detail: 20 of 31 model runs show a strong storm off the Northeast coast around Nov 14. Strongest run: 981 mb (lower = stronger).

freeze.title: First freeze in Buffalo
freeze.detail: Not yet this fall. 23 of 31 model runs freeze within 10 days, around Nov 16. Coldest run: 29°F.

arctic.title: Arctic air over Buffalo?
arctic.detail: 0 of 31 model runs bring air colder than 14°F about 5,000 ft up in the next 10 days. Coldest run: 15°F up there.

lakeeffect.title: Lake-effect snow setup?
lakeeffect.detail: 31 of 31 model runs get cold enough over Lake Erie (59°F water) for lake-effect snow around Nov 13. 100% show lake-effect rain showers.

seiche.title: Lake Erie seiche (sloshing) now
seiche.detail: Buffalo water level minus Toledo: +1.4 ft (Buffalo 2.8 ft above low water). 6+ ft difference = a big seiche.

waves.title: Lake Erie waves now
waves.detail: Eastern Lake Erie buoy: 5.2 ft waves. 8+ ft = big wave day.

aurora.title: Northern lights in the next 3 days?
aurora.detail: Highest forecast: Kp 3.0 around Nov 11. Kp 6+ = maybe visible from WNY, 7+ = good chance.

storms.title: Thunderstorm photo days
storms.detail: No thunderstorms expected in the next 3 days.

seichewind.title: Seiche / big-wave wind coming?
seichewind.detail: 0 of 31 model runs blow SW winds of 35+ mph down Lake Erie in the next 10 days. Strongest run: 37 mph.

seasmoke.title: Sea smoke (lake steam) mornings
seasmoke.detail: Needs Buffalo at 29°F or colder over 59°F water. 1 of 31 model runs get there around Nov 17.

fallsice.title: Niagara Falls ice?
fallsice.detail: 0 of 31 model runs bring 3 straight nights at 10°F or colder in the next 10 days.

recent.text: 🌊 Lake Erie is at a new record warm for Nov 9: 59.2°F, about 6°F warmer than normal. The record for this date is 58.9°F (2024). Warm lake water is fuel for lake-effect snow: when cold air blows over it, the lake adds heat and moisture, which can build heavier snow bands.

🥶 Cold pattern coming? The Arctic Oscillation (AO) measures how tightly cold air is held around the North Pole. The American model's average drops to -2.0 by Nov 12. A big negative number means the cold air is loosening and can spill south into the eastern U.S.

🌀 Nor'easter signal. A nor'easter is a strong storm that spins up off the East Coast and pulls in wind, rain and snow from the northeast. In 25 of 31 runs of the American weather model (81%), a powerful storm (pressure below 990 mb) forms off New England around Nov 14. Lower pressure means a stronger storm; the strongest run drops to 971 mb.

🗺️ NOAA's forecast for Nov 16–Nov 22 got more confident: Buffalo now has a 70% chance of being warmer than normal (before: 60% chance warmer than normal). This comes from NOAA's Climate Prediction Center, which forecasts whether the weeks ahead will run warmer or colder than usual.

In 18 of 31 runs of the American weather model (58%), a powerful storm (pressure below 990 mb) forms off New England around Nov 13. Lower pressure means a stronger storm; the strongest run drops to 968 mb.

🌀 Nor'easter signal. A nor'easter is a strong storm that spins up off the East Coast and pulls in wind, rain and snow from the northeast. In 11 of 31 runs of the American weather model (35%), a powerful storm (pressure below 990 mb) forms off New England around Nov 14. Lower pressure means a stronger storm; the strongest run drops to 979 mb.

❄️ Lake-effect snow setup. When cold air flows over the warmer lake, the lake heats and moistens it, and it rises into snow bands. Forecasters look for the lake to be about 23°F (13°C) warmer than the air 5,000 feet up, with that air cold enough for snow. In 27 of 31 runs of the American weather model (87%), that happens over Lake Erie around Nov 12. Wind direction decides who gets buried.

🌫️ Sea smoke photo morning. When air about 30°F colder than the lake sits over it, the lake "steams" like a hot bath, making wisps of fog called sea smoke. Lake Erie is 61°F and 20 of 31 model runs (65%) drop Buffalo to 31°F or colder around Nov 13. Best right at sunrise with light wind.

🧊 First freeze coming to Buffalo. Buffalo hasn't dropped to 32°F yet this fall. In 17 of 31 runs of the American weather model (55%), it freezes around Nov 12. The first freeze ends the growing season: frost kills off gardens and tender plants.

🌊 Lake Erie is at a new record warm for Nov 2: 61.0°F, about 6°F warmer than normal. The record for this date is 59.8°F (2024). Warm lake water is fuel for lake-effect snow: when cold air blows over it, the lake adds heat and moisture, which can build heavier snow bands.

❄️ Lake-effect snow setup. When cold air flows over the warmer lake, the lake heats and moistens it, and it rises into snow bands. Forecasters look for the lake to be about 23°F (13°C) warmer than the air 5,000 feet up, with that air cold enough for snow. In 14 of 31 runs of the American weather model (45%), that happens over Lake Erie around Nov 11. Wind direction decides who gets buried.

🌀 Nor'easter signal. A nor'easter is a strong storm that spins up off the East Coast and pulls in wind, rain and snow from the northeast. In 12 of 31 runs of the American weather model (39%), a powerful storm (pressure below 990 mb) forms off New England around Nov 10. Lower pressure means a stronger storm; the strongest run drops to 968 mb.

🌪️ The polar vortex may break down. The polar vortex is a huge spinning wind high above the Arctic that usually keeps the coldest air locked up north. In 29 of 31 runs of the American weather model (94%), that spin stops and reverses, as early as Nov 4. When that happens, Arctic air often spills south 1 to 3 weeks later, which can mean cold and snow for Buffalo. Yesterday it was 71%.
